verdicts.reason: A keeps a clean centred stack (logo, can in halo, badges, headline, CTA), but the badges move above the headline in reversed order, 'Swipe up to shop' is enlarged to body-copy size so it competes with the subhead, and about 90px at the bottom is dead space. B jams the stacked badges into the top-left corner and pushes the logo off to the right at a cramped, misaligned position; the halo circle sits off-centre to the left of the can, and there is a large empty gap between the can and the headline.

A crowds the logo into the top-right beside the stacked top-left badges, and the halo circle is offset left of the can, leaving a large empty gap under the product. B keeps the logo intact at the top, but it moves the halo behind the headline instead of the can, shrinks the can until it reads as minor, sits the badges below the product so they read out of order, and leaves dead bands above the can and below the CTA. Both are clearly flawed, and B is marginally better only because the logo is preserved.

A sets the badges neatly side by side at the top with a centred can and strong headline/CTA hierarchy, but it moves the logo to the bottom inside the repurposed halo circle, the CTA overlaps the circle's top edge, and the can loses its halo. B crowds the logo into the top-right beside the stacked badges, places the halo off-centre from the can, and leaves a large gap under the product.
